fatal_errors: The proposed PLD treatment is unrelated to the target intervention, which was a closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning, Bayesian-optimisation, and inverse-analysis campaign.
The starting Pt-Pd-Rh-Ru-Ce-Zr-O composition is invented and does not represent the explored five- to nineteen-element, 1 wt% catalyst space on La-doped gamma-alumina.
The asserted 30–40% NOx improvement and 50–70% reduction in platinum-group-metal consumption have no supporting evidence.
The ageing protocol and reaction conditions differ materially from the target's 900 °C, 5 h cyclic lean/rich water-containing ageing and specified multicomponent near-stoichiometric feed.

The surface-area and PGM-utilisation mechanism misses the observed element-specific electronic reconstruction, especially Cu–Pt cooperative adsorption; the target explicitly found that simple morphology or sintering was insufficient to explain performance.
The falsification experiment tests only overall performance and cannot distinguish the proposed morphology mechanism from compositional, electronic, dispersion, or support-interface effects.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad automotive-exhaust activity and durability problem and proposes a testable treated-versus-untreated comparison, but it does not reconstruct the material, intervention, mechanism, conditions, baseline, or outcomes of the target. Its quantitative predictions and PLD rationale are unsupported by cited evidence. The experiment also lacks matched-PGM controls, species-resolved light-off metrics, post-ageing comparison to the Pd benchmark, and structural measurements capable of causally testing the claimed mechanism.
